parsed.why: No trans criminalisation; trans-inclusive anti-discrimination with criminal penalties and 64% public support. But enforcement fails — LGBT murders uninvestigated (2017) and a 2024 survey documents widespread LGBTI exclusion. Protections paper-thin in practice.

Sodomy statute secondary, but police are documented perpetrators of rape, beating and sexual abuse of trans people; complaints reframed against victims; broader impunity for mob violence. Third-gender tradition and one sanctuary village do not offset state-tolerated targeting.

No criminalisation and functioning courts for trans litigants, but document process mostly absent, and 2024 reporting documents frequent physical and sexual harassment plus institutional discrimination against visibly trans people, with rising political hate speech.

Private conduct legal but public same-sex affection criminalised; no recognition or anti-discrimination law; documented arrests on false accusations and mistreatment and torture of LGBTQ people by law enforcement, under a climate of impunity. Community wholly concealed.

No criminalisation and a 2018 equality guarantee; only 2015 societal stigma documented, no police, violence, facilities or screening exposure recorded. Thin record: no protection shown operating, but no documented exposure either.
